newsitem.title: USA: LPC-Banks to lend Southern Peru Copper $600 mln.
newsitem.headline: LPC-Banks to lend Southern Peru Copper $600 mln.

text.p: NEW YORK, January 8 (LPC) - Six firms are leading a $600 million syndicated bank loan for Southern Peru Copper Corp, according to banking sources.
Arranging the deal are Chase Manhattan Bank, Citibank, Credit Suisse First Boston, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, J.P. Morgan & Co and Goldman Sachs, bankers said.
The loan will be structured as a $400 million, seven-year backstop facility and a $200 million, five-year working capital portion, several bankers said.

The $400 million tranche is priced at 175 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) if Southern Peru Copper receives an investment-grade rating, a banker said. Pricing rises to LIBOR plus 200 if the company is rated non-investment-grade, the banker added.
The five-year portion will be priced at 200 basis points over LIBOR, the source added.
Pricing on both tranches steps up by 25 basis points in years three and five, according to lenders.

In addition, Credit Suisse First Boston is leading a 10-year secured export note for Southern Peru Copper, according to banking sources. That deal will total at least $150 million, and may go as high as $400 million, bankers said.
